goal: rlo-sdk gets prompt-spec/1 (a semantic signature for one LLM task), a deterministic compiler and output checker built from the same spec, and rlo.optimize, which searches prompt variants against a deterministic metric under whatever budget the caller passes in. This is the base that ga's gemini plan prompt (T2) moves onto.
why: POL-2 T1 (CMD-AO3, BD-288). The user asked for prompt optimization and for prompts converted automatically from the semantic model. Today prompts are hand-written str.format text (ga/prompts.py, ga/gemini.py protocol()); there is no spec, no metric and no search. rev 2 (CMD-AO3 rev 2, BD-289): the user removed the free-tier limit; quota and rate limits belong to the integrating side, so rlo-sdk has no built-in quota or default cap.
refs: baseline SEMANTIC_MODEL.md section 1 (Opinion has no authority; terms)
ga-sdk 438a34a ga/gemini.py protocol() and PLAN_SCHEMA (the T2 consumer; read only)

scope.text: prompt-spec/1: a versioned, validated data form for one LLM task: goal; inputs, each with a name, a SEMANTIC_MODEL term (Observation, State, Evidence, DecisionContext, ...) and a basis; one output form with typed fields; rules; optional examples. Unknown terms or a missing basis are validation errors. The output is an Opinion (SEMANTIC_MODEL section 1), never State.

Compiler: (spec, variant, inputs) -> prompt text, deterministic and byte-stable for the same input on any OS (no dict-order, time, locale or random dependence). A variant may only change instruction wording, field order and few-shot picks; it cannot change the goal, inputs, output form or rules. The same spec also builds the output checker (parse + validate the answer), so the prompt and its parser cannot drift.

rlo.optimize: search over variants with a deterministic metric supplied by the caller; a train / held-out split; an optional call budget and an optional Governor that the caller passes in. With them, no call goes past the budget. Without them, the search simply runs to its end: there is no built-in quota and no default cap. A cache keyed by the hash of prompt text and case, so a repeated call costs nothing; resume across days and process restarts from the cache and a run record; a Telemetry record per call and per run. It adopts a variant only when its held-out score beats the base by a stated margin, else it keeps the base. An LLM-as-judge may not be the only metric. It returns a result; it never writes or deploys a prompt by itself.
The model call is an injected function. rlo-sdk does not import a provider SDK, read keys or hold any quota. The tests use a fake model and make no network calls.

done_when.text: Compiler: golden tests show byte-identical output for the same input twice and across a fresh process; a variant that tries to change goal, inputs, output form or rules is rejected; a checker built from the spec accepts the compiled prompt's well-formed answer and rejects a malformed one; mutations killed (field order taken from a set or dict, checker built from a different spec, unknown SEMANTIC_MODEL term accepted).

Optimize with a fake model: a better variant on held-out is adopted only above the margin, and a variant better only on train is not adopted; with a passed budget or Governor of N, the run stops at exactly N calls; with none passed, the run completes the whole search; a cache hit makes no call; a run killed midway resumes and ends with the same result and no repeated calls; Telemetry records exist; an LLM-only metric is refused; mutations killed (a passed budget not enforced, a default cap applied when none is passed, held-out leaked into train, margin ignored, cache key without the case).

Minor version bump. An empty venv installs rlo-sdk at your commit and pip check is clean; the full suite passes in a fresh clone; 0 network calls in tests. Report as report/2 in English on #11 with the commit sha, and a short API sketch for GA (T2).

changes.text: call cap enforced through the Governor -> optional budget and Governor passed in by the caller; no built-in quota or default cap (BD-289)
'T1 spends 0 Gemini requests' (a quota reason) -> rlo-sdk holds no quota; tests stay offline with a fake model
cap check applies to a passed budget; new check and mutation: no default cap when none is passed
